description: Single source of truth for every enumerated option this server advertises that is also an enumerated contract in agents-service. Each entry carries machine-readable provenance so a checker can re-derive the backend set from Java source without executing anything. Tools import these lists from backend-options.ts instead of restating literals, so drift is a one-line fix in one place.

rules.subset: Every value advertised by MCP must exist in the backend set. Advertising a value the backend rejects turns a tool call into a 400 the model cannot diagnose.
rules.uiReachability: Every value the Studio UI exposes to a human must also be reachable from MCP, otherwise the two clients cannot build the same artifact.
rules.declaredNarrowing: MCP may deliberately advertise fewer values than the backend accepts, but only where `narrowedFrom` explains why and the omitted values are not exposed by the UI.

widget.viewType.note: PUT /api/v2/widgets/{id} validates against this set; the narrower Java enum WidgetViewType only describes the snapshot payload shape and is NOT the request contract.

widget.binding.note: PULL and HYBRID additionally require a dataBindingId; the backend rejects the write without one.

backend.anchor: stateScope must be PUBLIC or PER_VISITOR

widget.stateScope.note: Chooses shared versus visitor-keyed state. It is not a workspace ACL and must never be described as one.

persistedButUnresolved.why: WidgetWizardService persists sourceType STUDIO_OPERATIONS, but no WidgetDataSourceAdapter registers that type, so WidgetDataBindingResolver.resolve returns empty and /state falls back to the last stored snapshot. Advertise it (the wizard really writes it) and say plainly that a PULL read will not resolve until an adapter exists.

widget.bindingSourceType.note: The WidgetDataBinding javadoc also names MODULE and EXECUTION. No adapter implements either, so they are not advertised.

narrowedFrom.why: Those three channels are driven by the presenter and browser-voice subsystems, not by the chatflow session API this server calls, and the Studio UI does not offer them on a chatflow session either.

deploy.option.note: The wire values are what the UI sends and what DeployOption.fromWire accepts; the short aliases are a convenience this server maps before the request leaves.

deploy.phase.note: GET /v2/workflows/{id}/deploy/{deploymentId}/status returns a DeploymentStatusEvent carrying both `phase` and an authoritative `terminal` boolean. Prefer `terminal`: derivePhase maps STOPPING and TERMINATING to phase TERMINATED while isTerminal still reports false, so phase alone would call a shutting-down deployment finished.

narrowedFrom.why: FrameworkConfig registers six frameworks, but AppWizardService defaults every path to REACT_VITE and the Studio applications surface offers no other choice, so the other five are unexercised. Advertising them would invite builds nobody has verified.
